subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Overconfidence Bias
description: A quick win: understand Overconfidence Bias.

hook.text: When people say they are 90% confident in an answer, they are right about 70% of the time.

buildup.text: CEOs, doctors, and generals display the same pattern. Expertise reduces overconfidence slightly but never eliminates it.

discovery.text: Overconfidence drove the 2008 crisis. Banks believed their risk models were accurate.

twist.text: Some overconfidence is useful. Entrepreneurs who accurately knew the odds of failure would never start.

climax.text: Overconfidence is dangerous in high-stakes decisions but useful for motivation.

punchline.text: Ninety percent sure? Probably seventy percent right.

quiz.question: Why is overconfidence sometimes useful?
options: It motivates action, as entrepreneurs who knew true failure odds might never start
